blocks.text: Remembering is a painful task. A sharp point deep in the hollow of the back, it grabs us by the throat with its large hands. Then it tightens. Even happy memories carry their own scent of pain, because they no longer exist. The raw memory was once so simple. But time made you lose your story. You drift. Melancholic. Strange. I do not remember what you said. I remember there was water. Holding your hand to fall asleep. An ice cream on the pavement. A note left on the table. I do not want it to fade away. The further I go, the less taste the madeleine has. Besides, was it ever really a madeleine? I no longer know. Is it intact memory, or forgetting itself, that does not exist? I do not know. There are images that keep changing places. Shapes that persist for too long. Sometimes traces I never asked for. Often fragments I have lost. So I continue. Trying to hold onto what is disintegrating, and despite myself, turning it into an inventory of erasure. A mental texture repeating itself poorly. A construction of uncertainty. Or what remains of it.
